instructions: Answer Question 1 (compulsory) and any three of Questions 2 to 6. For each part, write your answer first, then reveal the model answer and tick the marking points you got.

questions.title: Simulating a classroom delivery robot
questions.stem: A group of students is designing a small robot to deliver books between classrooms. Before building it, they test the design in simulation software.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State two benefits of simulating the robot before building it.
parts.model:
1. It saves cost because no hardware is damaged or wasted while testing ideas.
2. Testing is faster, safe and repeatable: designs can be changed and re-run many times without risk.

points.text: Saves cost / no damaged or wasted hardware
Faster, safer or repeatable testing (easy to change and re-test)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Apart from movement, state two other features of the robot that can be tested in the simulation.
parts.model: Any two of: sensor placement and performance, motor torque and speed, battery use, payload (how much it can carry), turning radius, obstacle avoidance.

points.text: First valid feature (sensors, motor torque/speed, battery, payload, turning radius, obstacle avoidance)

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: In the simulation the robot keeps hitting the walls when turning in narrow corridors. State one design cause.
parts.model: Any one of: turning radius too large or wheelbase too long; blind spots at the sides because of sensor placement; sensor range too short; motors respond too slowly.

points.text: One valid design cause (turning radius, wheelbase, sensor placement or range, slow motor response)

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: The chassis will be 3D printed. Name one material used by each type of printer: FDM and SLA.
parts.model:
FDM: PLA (or ABS, PETG).
SLA: photopolymer resin.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Which printer is better for the robot chassis?
parts.model: FDM.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: Give a reason for your answer in (d)(ii).
parts.model: FDM parts are tougher and more impact resistant, cheaper, and the printer has a larger build volume. SLA resin parts are brittle and could crack when the robot bumps into things.

points.text: FDM is tougher / impact resistant / cheaper / larger build volume
SLA resin is brittle (or comparison made)

questions.title: Four-legged walking robot
questions.stem: A four-legged walking robot of mass 8 kg is driven by cranks and is designed to cross rocky terrain.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State one advantage of legs over wheels on rocky terrain.
parts.model: Legs can step over rocks and gaps and keep traction (grip) on uneven ground, where wheels would get stuck or slip.

points.text: Steps over rocks or gaps / keeps traction on uneven ground

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate the load on each leg when the robot stands on all four legs. (g = 9.8 m/s²)
parts.model:
W = mg = 8 × 9.8 = 78.4 N
Load per leg = 78.4 ÷ 4 = 19.6 N (20 N if g = 10 m/s²)

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Each crank motor turns at 0.5 rev/s and the robot moves 80 mm per rotation. How far does it travel in 3 minutes?
parts.model:
Rotations = 0.5 × 180 s = 90
Distance = 90 × 80 mm = 7200 mm = 7.2 m

points.text: Converts 3 min to 180 s (and 80 mm to 0.08 m)

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Counterweights are added to lower the robot's centre of gravity. Discuss the effect of this change.
parts.model:
Benefit: a lower centre of gravity makes the robot more stable and it resists tipping over on rocks.
Drawback: the extra mass increases the load on the motors, drains the battery faster and makes the robot slower.

points.text: More mass means more motor load or battery drain

questions.title: Autonomous delivery vehicle
questions.stem: An autonomous delivery vehicle uses closed-loop control. It must reach a delivery point 10 m away and stop accurately.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by a closed-loop system.
parts.model: A closed-loop system uses sensor feedback: it measures the actual output, compares it with the desired value (setpoint) and corrects the error.

points.text: Compares actual output with setpoint and corrects the error

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: If the vehicle moves at 0.5 m/s, how long does it take to travel 10 m?

points.text: t = d ÷ v with correct substitution

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Draw a flowchart for the vehicle: it follows a pre-defined path, checks whether it has reached its destination, reads an obstacle sensor at junctions, and stops and waits if an obstacle is detected.
parts.model: Start → Follow pre-defined path → Destination reached? (Yes → Stop at destination; No → Read obstacle sensor) → At a junction? (No → back to Follow path; Yes → Obstacle detected?) → Obstacle detected? (No → back to Follow path; Yes → Stop motors and wait → back to Read obstacle sensor).

points.text: Yes and No branches labelled and loops back correctly

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain how a PID controller helps the vehicle stop accurately at the delivery point.
parts.model:
P: the motor command is proportional to the remaining distance, so it slows as it gets close.
I: removes any steady error so it does not stop short.
D: damps overshoot and oscillation so it does not roll past.
The gains are tuned using encoder feedback.

questions.title: Logic circuit
questions.stem: In a logic circuit, inputs X and NOT Y feed AND gate 1. Inputs Y and Z feed AND gate 2. The outputs of the two AND gates feed an XOR gate whose output is F.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Write the Boolean expression for F.
parts.model: F = XY' ⊕ YZ

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Complete the truth table for the circuit, with columns X, Y, Z, XY', YZ and F.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: State two reasons why Boolean algebra is important in robotics.
parts.model:
1. It simplifies logic circuits, so fewer gates are needed, which makes circuits cheaper, smaller and faster.
2. It allows precise design and analysis of digital logic and robot decisions.

points.text: Precise design and analysis of logic / robot decisions

questions.title: Cams, algorithms and the industrial revolution
questions.stem: A robot uses an eccentric cam to lift a part. Its control program sometimes misbehaves.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: An eccentric cam of eccentricity r = 4 cm rotates through 90°. Using s = r(1 − cos θ), calculate the follower lift.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State one design consideration for smooth cam operation.
parts.model: Any one of: a smooth cam profile, a roller follower, a return spring, lubrication, correct alignment.

points.text: One valid consideration (smooth profile, roller follower, spring, lubrication, alignment)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by an algorithm flaw.
parts.model: A logic or sequence error in the program that makes the robot behave wrongly even though the hardware is working correctly.

points.text: Logic or sequence error in the program
Causes wrong behaviour even though hardware works

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: State two technological advancements of the second industrial revolution.
parts.model: Any two of: electricity, assembly line mass production, Bessemer steel process, telephone or telegraph, internal combustion engine.

questions.title: Calibrating a temperature sensor
questions.stem: A robot's temperature sensor reads a few degrees different from the actual temperature.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: What is meant by calibration?
parts.model: Comparing the sensor's readings with a known accurate reference and adjusting the readings to match it.

points.text: Compare with a known accurate reference

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the steps of a one-point calibration.
parts.model:
1. Put the sensor and a reference thermometer in the same stable environment.
2. Record both readings and calculate offset = reference − sensor.
3. Apply the offset in the code and re-test.

points.text: Same stable environment as a reference thermometer
Apply offset in code and re-test

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Describe how the sensor signal is processed by the microcontroller.
parts.model: Sensor output voltage → ADC converts it to a number 0 to 1023 → number converted to °C → offset applied (and readings averaged) → value used for decisions.

points.text: ADC converts voltage to a number 0 to 1023
Converted to °C and offset applied / averaged

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: How can the calibration be verified?
parts.model: Compare the corrected readings against a certified thermometer at different real temperatures and over a period of time.
